To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have made a comprehensive comparative transcriptional analysis of DC and macrophage subsets across the immune system and identified transcriptional programs that regulate DC commitment, functional specialization and homeostasis.
we identified transcription factors that regulate DC development and function and that we identified a transcriptional signature of DCs that may control self-tolerance.
we identified candidate transcriptional activator genes that are required for the differentiation of DCs in the steady-state and in the presence of inflammation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transcriptional regulation and functional diversity of dendritic cells.
understanding the transcriptional networks controlling DC differentiation and function.
understanding the molecular basis of dendritic cell (DC) development and function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study has identified the transcriptional program of DCs, which may help to understand the development, function and homeostasis of DCs in the steady state.

the transcriptional network controlling the DC lineage commitment has been deciphered, and the transcriptional program controlling DC functional specialization has been identified, at least in the steady state.
the transcriptional network that controls DC differentiation, maturation, and function is complex, highly interconnected, and tightly controlled by the tissue environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transcriptional program of the DC lineage has been deciphered and that this program is highly conserved across the immune system.
we have identified transcriptional regulators involved in the commitment and functional specialization in DCs.

our data suggest that the transcription factors that are involved in the commitment and differentiation of the DC lineages are not only restricted to the transcription factors that we identified in our analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DCs are a heterogeneous population of cells, and their functional diversity may be controlled by a complex network of transcription factors.

transcriptional regulation of DC development and functional specialization is a complex process that involves the interplay of multiple factors, including lineage-specific transcription factors, epigenetic modifications and microRNAs.

DCs in different tissues are molecularly distinct from each other and from macrophages, and this molecular diversity is controlled by tissue-specific transcriptional programs that are likely to be critical in maintaining tolerance to tissue antigens.
